assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic activity of the processed peptide) underpins a drug class that has transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment. Discovery-to-medicine arc is exceptionally clear and the clinical impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and processing of GLP-1), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotropic GLP-2, translational work) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) are the strongest fit among the credited names. Knudsen's liraglutide/semaglutide development is an industrial contribution that could alternatively be recognized; credit among these is contested and no configuration is uncontroversial.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic work is decades old and independently confirmed, and the clinical outcomes in diabetes, weight and cardiovascular risk are now firmly established; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority dispute surrounding Mojsov versus other early peptide contributors, including people not on the supplied list
Whether academic physiology or drug development (Knudsen) should be weighted more
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have opened a new therapeutic modality; originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain each led the design of costimulated CAR constructs and early clinical translation. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR trials are important, but I judge the decisive CAR engineering contributions to sit with June and Sadelain. Foundational receptor-chimera work by others (not on the supplied list) leaves credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multiple independent clinical confirmations; long-term remission data are mature for several indications, while solid tumours and toxicities remain open.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric-receptor concept credit lies partly with people not in the credited names
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and safety issues such as cytokine release and secondary malignancy

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis democratized genome-scale measurement, enabling human genetics, cancer genomics, transcriptomics and single-cell biology. The enabling impact across all of biomedicine is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the reversible-terminator, single-molecule-array approach that became the dominant platform; Mayer contributed key early clusters-on-surface concepts. Other platform developers (e.g. pyrosequencing and polony approaches) are outside the supplied names, so a fair configuration is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Technology is thoroughly validated and ubiquitous; recognition is mature. As a methods prize it is closer to the Chemistry committee's typical remit but fits the physiology-or-medicine impact criterion.
uncertainties: Whether a technology invention is best framed as a medicine discovery
Competing platform origins and intellectual-property history complicate attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a novel intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus (Ire1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK), with consequences for diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A conceptually original, well-defined discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified the core Ire1-mediated pathway in yeast and its mammalian counterpart; the pairing is a clean and plausible two-person prize. Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Kaufman, Schekman-era genetics, not on the supplied list) leave some residual allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Pathway is highly confirmed and conserved over three decades; therapeutic translation is still emerging, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Additional key contributors outside the supplied names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR and the mTORC1/2 pathway as the central regulator of cell growth in response to nutrients and growth factors is a foundational discovery with implications for cancer, metabolism, immunity and aging; rapamycin biology gives it clinical reach.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined its role in growth control; Sabatini contributed decisive mammalian mTOR pathway mechanisms (raptor, rictor, nutrient sensing). Schreiber's chemical-genetic work on FKBP-rapamycin is relevant, and credit around mTOR discovery in mammals (including Sabatini and Sabers/Brown-era work) is not fully settled by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well-confirmed and broadly impactful; rapamycin analogues are clinically used. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation between yeast genetics, mammalian mTOR discovery and chemical biology
Some people important to the mTOR story are not in the credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5 stem-cell identification and long-term culture of adult-stem-cell-derived organoids created a new experimental system for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalized medicine. A strong enabling platform with biological insight.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader; Sato executed the decisive organoid derivation. A two-person configuration is clean, though earlier tissue culture and embryonic-stem-cell organoid work by others is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently reproduced across tissues; some clinical applications are still maturing, so the recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the platform versus mechanistic discovery
Clinical utility for patient-specific therapy is still being established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics enabled causal, cell-type-specific control of neural circuits and has transformed neuroscience; the discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use as neuronal actuators is a conceptually clear and widely validated advance.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg, who is credited but constrained by the three-name limit) discovered and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenböck established their neuronal application. Allocation among six credited names is the central difficulty, and I select a mix of discovery and application without resolving it.
assessment.maturity: Technology has been adopted in thousands of laboratories and has entered early clinical use in vision restoration; recognition is well matured.
uncertainties: Six credible contributors and a three-laureate limit make a fair configuration difficult
Primarily a research tool with limited therapeutic impact so far

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense-oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a lethal childhood disease into a treatable one and validated splicing modulation as a therapeutic strategy, linking RNA biology with clinical benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's mechanistic splicing work and Bennett's oligonucleotide chemistry and development jointly underlie the therapy; the pairing is clean. Contributions from the Singh/Androphy and Hua/Krainer groups and the identification of SMN2 and SMN1 as the genetic basis are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy confirmed by randomized trials and long-term follow-up, with independent replication of the platform; the field is still young, so the recognition may be somewhat early relative to others.
uncertainties: Credit for the target identification and intronic silencer discovery is distributed beyond the supplied names
Long-term outcomes and treatment timing questions remain
